2	Send every Agent chat from an append-only record, so provider caches hit
3	
4	Each request a chat sends is now the record of everything it sent
5	before, byte for byte, plus what this turn adds. Before, the host
6	rebuilt the history on every request from the chat's messages, and
7	seven things changed earlier bytes between requests: a reminder added
8	at the front, a 64 KiB rolling trim, a 16 KiB cut of old tool results,
9	skills dropped after their turn, app notes rewritten in place, workspace
10	and picture stripping, and an unstable tool list. Each one invalidated
11	the provider's prompt cache from that byte on.
12	
13	What changed in the Agent:
14	- ProjectStateDocument keeps a per-chat ChatRecord of the items sent,
15	  in the wire format they were sent in; pictures are kept beside it
16	  under chats/<conversation>/ and read back as sent. Items join the
17	  record only once the provider has accepted the request, so a refused
18	  request leaves no trace.
19	- ProviderAgent renders that record on every request and appends the
20	  turn's own items. A chat talks in one wire format; picking a model of
21	  another format fails the turn with chat_format_fixed.
22	- Fired skills and app notes go as operator-role messages (an in-array
23	  system message on Anthropic, a developer item on Responses) and stay
24	  in the record. On a direct Anthropic connection a skill is scoped to
25	  its own request with clear_at; through the gateway and on Responses it
26	  stays in place.
27	- Responses requests carry a per-chat prompt_cache_key; object_import is
28	  offered on every turn so the tool list never changes; the file-load
29	  reminder, the rolling trim and the result cut are gone.
30	- A chat-title request keeps nothing in the record.
31	- A tool call's outcome is announced once, after the save that follows
32	  it, and the MCP bridge builds with the project's Asio setting so its
33	  tests no longer hang.
34	
35	Tests: a [history-prefix] guard checks on both codecs that every request
36	of a turn opens with the whole previous request. The shell harness logs
37	every request body as posted (--request-log) and runs a three-chat live
38	journey on either provider; prefix_check.py reports the first differing
39	byte between consecutive bodies. The prompt suite is re-recorded on the
40	record, with its "skill sent once" checks restated as "appended once,
41	then replayed", and assertions across four test layers now read tool
42	lists, model ids and profile values from the app instead of copies.

482	Print history: record every G-code that leaves a project, show it, print it again
483	
484	One record per G-code that left a project replaces the Sent events and
485	physical prints, which nothing outside tests ever wrote. It is shown on one
486	Print history screen, and any recorded G-code can be printed again from the
487	file the project kept. Nothing records, badges or draws a failure: a
488	printer reports a person's stop and a failed print the same way, so a print
489	that ended early simply never finishes. Slicing writes nothing.
490	
491	The record (Agent/ManufacturingHistory, Agent/ProjectStateDocument)
492	- Keyed by the SHA-256 of the plate's sliced G-code, so the same slice
493	  exported and sent is one record. It holds where the G-code went (exports
494	  with the exported file's own hash; sends with the printer's name, whether
495	  the send started the print, when the transport confirmed it, and for a
496	  Bambu send the hash of the package it uploaded) and the prints the
497	  printer reported: started, finished. It also holds the slice's estimates
498	  and layer count, the presets, and the chat item it followed.
499	- A copy of each G-code that leaves is kept at <project>/gcode/<hash>.gcode,
500	  the newest 20 per project. A Bambu print also keeps the .gcode.3mf it
501	  uploaded, byte for byte (and for a cloud printer the config 3MF it also
502	  sent), pruned with its G-code.
503	- A document holding the old "sent" and "physicalPrints" arrays loads and
504	  drops them (no shipped build wrote them).
505	
506	Writers (Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder)
507	- Exports (OrcaSlicer's own and the export_file tool's) through the new
508	  EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED; Bambu prints and uploads through the jobs' finished
509	  events while their dialog is showing; print-host uploads through the
510	  queue's new enqueue observer and the queue dialog's progress at 100.
511	- Bambu printers are polled every two seconds whatever is on screen;
512	  Agent/PrintOutcomeTracker decides which report belongs to which send, and
513	  a finish of a project that is not open is written into its saved
514	  document. Print hosts record sends only.
515	
516	Print history (HomeUI, Home/PrintHistory, Home/OrcaHomeBackend)
517	- A second screen of the Home page: one entry per G-code, grouped by day,
518	  with a row per destination (an export: matches, changed outside JusPrin,
519	  not found; a send: delivery and whether it started) and per print
520	  (Printing with its progress, Finished; a stopped one shows only when it
521	  started). Project and printer are removable filter chips over one list,
522	  with a search box. Its bar is Back and the title: Preferences is reached
523	  from the title bar's menu and Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).
524	- Ways in: a link in the gallery header, a line on each project card and
525	  printer card, one row on the project pane's Project tab (replacing its
526	  old Print history view), and a "history" link on each chat marker. Back
527	  returns to where it was opened from.
528	- Open in chat opens the project and scrolls its chat to the marker
529	  (reveal_item). Export... writes the kept copy and records it; Export again
530	  on a changed file writes a new file beside it, never over it.
531	- The chat shows one marker line where a G-code left, in place of the

534	Print again, and print_dialog_open

1682	on another model, hosts or judge. The exit code is 1 when a case is marked
1683	worse; --must-pass keeps the old rule. --results saves a run in the
1684	baseline's form, --compare compares a saved run without sending anything,
1685	and --record-baseline makes a full run (or a saved one) the new baseline.
1686	The README says when to re-record: after Kenneth accepts a deliberate
1687	change, or when the model, hosts or judge change. test_steps.py checks the
1688	marking, the recording and that both files name exactly the current cases.

1690	Removing setup_record's fields
1691

1693	requirement names the model chose, each with a value, a question or an
1694	assumed flag. They are removed end to end, because:

1704	  as a weight limit and metres as minutes, summed ranges, and worked only in

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. JusPrin turns `single_instance` on at every start; its instance lock
lives in the data directory, so a scratch `--datadir` runs as its own instance
beside another JusPrin. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Where each request first differs from the chat's previous one.

Reads a --request-log directory (tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp) and, for
consecutive bodies of one chat, prints the first differing byte and the JSON
path there. Title requests carry no "tools", so they are paired only with each
other. --ignore-cache-control drops Anthropic's breakpoint, which moves to the
newest user content on every request, before comparing.

Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py LOG_DIR [--ignore-cache-control]
"""

import json, pathlib, re, sys


def common_prefix(a, b):
    lo, hi = 0, min(len(a), len(b))  # by halving, as slices compare at C speed
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
        lo, hi = (mid, hi) if a[:mid] == b[:mid] else (lo, mid - 1)
    return lo

---
name: windows-baseline-2026-11-01
description: "Windows results at jusprin-newui b08a307459: which harness and test failures are known, why, and how to run a real chat offline against a local stand-in model"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Full Windows pass on 2026-11-01 at `b08a307459` (Release, `C:\src\JusPrin\build`, ALL_BUILD about 35 minutes). Scripts are in `C:\b\wk7`.

Known failures at that commit, not caused by anything newer:
- `ALL_BUILD` fails: `shell_theme_tests` (`auto near` clashes with the Windows `near` macro, test_shell_theme.cpp:365) and `agent_live_tests` (b08a removed `AgentConversationContext`, test_provider_live.cpp still uses it). Other targets still link. Remove this line once fixed.
- Default shell harness, 9 checks: the 4 autosave checks, the 2 `agent_panel_columns_tile_*`, and `not_connected_ring_reads_as_dashed`, `no_colour_ring_reads_as_dashed`, `outline_button_sits_on_whole_pixels_at_2x`. Those last three are the instrument: on Windows `snapshot(2.0)` draws at 1x into the top-left quarter of a 2x bitmap, at 100% and 200% display scale alike.
- `--printer-setup` stalls after `printer_panel_shows_its_offer`: Preferences never connects when opened inside the harness's `wait_for` wxYield. The real app's same button works. Exact cause not proven.
- `--home-live` stalls at `home_live_page_shows_online`: Home v3 draws an idle printer as `.printer-chip`, and the harness reads the old card.
- `--project-prompt-requests` fails 9 `*_appends_<skill>` checks: skillParser.ts keeps CRLF from a Windows checkout, so the page sends CRLF skill text. The harness comment saying the page sends LF is wrong on Windows. Same cause as the 2 AgentUI vitest skills failures and the known `pick_attachment` CRLF failure's family.
- ctest: PlaceholderParser coFloatsOrPercents segfault and `pick_attachment` previewText. Workspace harness: `second_model_dropped`, `model_added_to_a_project_is_an_edit`.
- `tests/project_prompt/test_claude_cli.py` fails on Windows: `claude_cli.py` hard-codes `dir="/tmp"`.

Real chat with no provider: `C:\b\wk7\mock.mjs` is a local Responses API stand-in. Start the app with `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/responses` and a placeholder key in the scratch `JusPrin2.conf` (`conf-agent.mjs`: the file ends in an MD5 line, a hand edit without it is discarded). `chat.mjs` then drives the page with real typed input and wheel events over DevTools.

**Why:** Saves the next Windows pass from re-diagnosing these.
**How to apply:** Compare new failures against this list, and re-check anything here before quoting it, since fixes may have landed. See [[windows-build-machine]], [[native-ui-synthetic-input-and-capture]].

The RDP session can change display scale mid-run when Kenneth reconnects (100% to 200% on 2026-11-01). Whole-screen capture coordinates change with it, so re-read `query session` and the screen size if a click misses.

content.text:
The past week's commits work on Windows along the main path, and I found nothing that blocks normal use once a printer is set up. Testing did turn up two test programs that don't compile, two display bugs and a Slice block on new data folders. Nothing is fixed or committed, and the working tree is clean.

I pulled `jusprin-newui` up to `b08a307459`. There are 35 commits from the past 7 days, not the 34 I said earlier, and I tested them together at the latest commit rather than one at a time.

## What the week's commits do
- **Agent chat:** each request now re-sends the chat exactly as sent before plus the new part, so provider caches hit. Each chat is also named to JusPrin's gateway. The chat scrolls to your message and offers "Jump to latest", and every action in a turn's log opens into its details.
- **Print history:** a new screen records every G-code that leaves a project and can print it again.
- **Home and startup:** there's a new Home page, and the app starts there without reopening a project or asking to sync the printer. A new data folder now shows the first-run screen instead of an error.
- **Prepare:** the header menu is reorganised, the setup card is split in two, and the printer chip says "from the file". Classic view now has a way back, and automatic slicing was removed.
- **Slice warnings:** the issue chip, the agent and Check print now report the same warnings.
- **Project reloads:** reloading a checkpoint no longer shows Orca's dialogs or renames presets, and hidden presets the project uses are now accepted.
- **Design and docs:** button heights and text sizes changed, and the prompt tests now compare against a stored baseline. Three commits are docs only.

## What I checked in the running app
- **First run:** a new data folder shows the first-run screen with no error, and after a restart the app opens on Home with the project listed.
- **Main path:** with Bambu profiles and the fake printer, `Tape_4_3MF.3mf` shows "from the file" and slices. Check print reads "Tape_4_3MF · sliced for Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle".
- **Chat:** I ran a real chat against a local stand-in for the model, using real mouse-wheel input.
  - Following the answer, holding your place when you scroll up, jumping back to your message and "Jump to latest" all behaved as designed.
  - A failed action opened into its full details.
  - In the offline request test, all 4,171 consecutive request pairs were clean appends.
- **Automated tests:**
  - Native tests: 965 of 967 pass; both failures were already known on this machine.
  - Home page tests: all pass.
  - Agent page tests: 620 of 622 pass; the 2 failures are the line-ending issue below.
  - UI harness modes: 17 of 20 run clean.

## Problems in the app
1. **The print-issue list and bubble are cut off at 200% display scale on Windows.** The text doubles but the box stays its 100% width, so lines end in "Relative extruder addres…". This code dates from 12 October, so it isn't from this week.
2. **"From the file" doesn't appear on a data folder with no Bambu profiles.** After opening the Bambu 3MF, the chip shows "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3…" as if it were your own printer. The rule reads a copy of the preset that doesn't carry its "came from a project" flag.
3. **On that same new data folder, Slice is blocked.** The error is "Relative extruder addressing requires resetting…", because the exemption for Bambu printers depends on the profiles being installed. A new user who opens a MakerWorld file first would hit this. It's your call whether to fix it, and I couldn't tell whether upstream behaves the same way, because blame stops at the fork's import commit.

Two smaller things:
- A project on OrcaSlicer's placeholder "Default Printer" says "3 settings changed" after reopening with no edits; All settings lists only one, a difference in a space. It doesn't happen on a Bambu printer.
- At 100% scale the "Not connected" ring looks lumpy rather than dashed; at 200% it looks right.

## Problems in the tests
- **Two test programs don't compile:**
  - `shell_theme_tests` names a variable `near`, which Windows reserves (`e5043249dc`). With a temporary rename, since reverted, it built and passed.
  - `agent_live_tests` still uses a type that `b08a307459` removed, so it should fail on every platform.
- **Two harness modes hang, but the app is fine:**
  - `--home-live` still looks for the old printer card; Home v3 draws an idle printer as a chip. Its later steps never ran.
  - `--printer-setup` stalls when it opens Preferences from the printer chat. That same button works in the real app; the exact cause in the harness isn't proven.
- **Three pixel checks can't pass on Windows:** the harness's "2x" picture is really drawn at 1x, so the two ring checks and the 2x outline check measure the wrong thing.
- **Skill text keeps Windows line endings:** a page built on Windows sends skills with those endings. That explains the 9 failed checks in the prompt request run and the 2 Agent page failures. Those request bytes will also differ from a Mac build's.

## Not tested
- **Live providers and the real gateway:** those runs are billed and need your approval, so I didn't run them. The chat-name header only has unit tests.
- **Real hardware and cloud:** no live Bambu printer and no cloud sends.
- **macOS-only fixes:** `660f845e00` and `2d3fc8157a` fix macOS crashes, so a pass here says nothing about them.

Logs and screenshots are in `C:\b\wk7`.
Compile breaks only

content.text:
Three of the five bugs need fixing: the Slice block on a new data folder, the cut-off print issues, and the missing "from the file" mark. The other two can wait. The screenshots are sent, numbered to match the list below. None of these bugs is fixed yet.

## Fix these
**3. Slice is blocked on a new data folder (fix first).** This is the worst one, because it can stop a new user's first print.
- **What happens:** someone opens a Bambu 3MF before setting up a printer, and Slice stays grey with an error about "Relative extruder addressing" and `G92 E0`. They can't act on that message. The same file sliced fine once Bambu profiles were installed.
- **Why:** OrcaSlicer's check skips Bambu printers, but it can't recognise this one without the profiles.
- **Fix:** when a 3MF names a printer maker whose profiles aren't installed, install them on open. That also shows the correct chip. A plain model on the placeholder "Default Printer" hits the same error, so there the message should say to add a printer.

**1. Print issues are cut off above 100% display scale on Windows (screenshots 1a, 1b).**
- **What happens:** warnings end mid-word ("Relative extruder addres…") and the "Why" label is clipped to "Wh". Windows laptops commonly run above 100%, and this panel exists to explain problems.
- **Why:** the text doubles at 200% but the box keeps its 100% width. OrcaSlicer's scale value appears to stay at 1 on Windows; the box widths I measured match that, but I didn't read the value directly.
- **Fix:** small, as only the panel's scale calculation should need to change. This dates from 12 October, not this week.

**2. "From the file" is missing on that same new data folder (screenshots 2a, 2b).** The chip shows "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3…" as if it were your own printer, and the menu treats it that way too. Bug 3's fix hides this for known printer makers, but a custom printer inside a 3MF would still get it. This also looks like a small fix: the rule needs to check the stored preset, which carries the "came from a project" flag.

## Leave these for now
**4. "3 settings changed" on a project nobody edited (screenshots 4a, 4b).** Only one setting is listed, and it differs by a single space. I only saw this on the placeholder printer, where Slice is blocked anyway; a reopened project on a Bambu printer showed no false count. One open question is that the count and the list disagree, so it's worth checking when that code is next touched.

**5. The "Not connected" ring looks solid at 100% (screenshot 5).** At 8 pixels there's no room for dashes, and it looks right at 200%. "Not connected" is written right beside it, so nothing is lost. The left half of that picture is the harness's 100% drawing, because this session is now at 200%.

## Compile fixes
Both test programs now build on Windows; the changes are uncommitted.
- **`shell_theme_tests`:** the clashing variable is renamed, and all of its tests pass.
- **`agent_live_tests`:** I rewrote its two out-of-date cases for the new chat record.
  - The history case now replays that record.
  - The title case now sends only the person's words, as the app does. That removes its two old scenarios (a replayed call and a chat opening on the assistant), since titles no longer receive a conversation.

Both rewritten cases pass against a local stand-in, but I didn't run them against real Anthropic because those runs are billed. The stand-in sends no thinking blocks, so replaying thinking wasn't exercised.

195-Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
196-exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and

200-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
201-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
202-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
203-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
204-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
205-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
206-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
207-   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
208-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.

210-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a

212-   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already

214-   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
215-   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.

13	For line numbers you need a tree with debug info. Configure with
14	`"-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE=/MD /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG /Z7"`, the same for C, and `"-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_RELEASE=/DEBUG:FULL /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF"` (example: `C:\b\ckp-build.cmd`). **Keep `/MD`.** Overriding the flags without it compiles everything `/MT`, and the link fails only at the very end with `LNK2038 RuntimeLibrary mismatch` against opencv/libcurl, after a 40-minute build. `SLIC3R_MSVC_PDB` is declared in CMakeLists.txt but nothing reads it.
15	
16	Quick triage without any of this: the event-log fault offset in a system DLL maps to a function via `dumpbin /exports <dll>` (the nearest export at or below the offset). ucrtbase `0x2a341` is `strlen+0x31`, meaning a null or bad `char*`.
17	
18	Run harnesses with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardError` rather than PowerShell `2>`. A PowerShell native-command redirect writes the file only when the process exits, so a hung run shows a 0-byte log. Visible windows of a stuck process can be listed with `C:\b\ckp-windows.ps1 -ProcessId <pid>` (a `#32770` titled 引导_P21 is OrcaSlicer's setup guide left open).

Creating any GL canvas leaves no context current, so GL work right after constructing a canvas needs an explicit make-current first. Upstream's helper for this is `GLCanvas3D::_set_shown_canvas_current`.

12	
13	**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.
14	
15	**How to apply:**
16	- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
17	- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
18	- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
19	- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
20	- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
21	- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.

# Before and after for bug 1, from the real app at 200%, same file and same issue.
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Drawing
$p = Get-Process orca-slicer -EA SilentlyContinue
if ($p) { $p.CloseMainWindow() | Out-Null; if (-not $p.WaitForExit(30000)) { Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force } }
$red = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(214, 40, 40); $green = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(30, 130, 76)
$ink = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(25, 25, 30); $grey = [System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(80, 80, 90)
$title = New-Object System.Drawing.Font 'Segoe UI Semibold', 30
$body = New-Object System.Drawing.Font 'Segoe UI', 21
$tag = New-Object System.Drawing.Font 'Segoe UI Semibold', 21
$panels = @(
  @{ F = 'C:\b\wk7\bugs\1a-issue-bubble-clipped.png'; C = @(300, 100, 340, 420); T = 'BEFORE: one issue open'; Ok = $false; X = 40; Y = 200 },
  @{ F = 'C:\b\wk7\fixed\bubble2-crop.png'; C = @(460, 490, 620, 490); T = 'AFTER: the same issue'; Ok = $true; X = 460; Y = 200 },
  @{ F = 'C:\b\wk7\bugs\1b-issue-list-clipped.png'; C = @(240, 110, 410, 210); T = 'BEFORE: the list'; Ok = $false; X = 40; Y = 770 },
  @{ F = 'C:\b\wk7\fixed\list-crop.png'; C = @(250, 180, 680, 330); T = 'AFTER: the list'; Ok = $true; X = 460; Y = 770 }
)
$bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap 1180, 1190
$g = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bmp)
$g.Clear([System.Drawing.Color]::White); $g.SmoothingMode = 'AntiAlias'; $g.TextRenderingHint = 'AntiAliasGridFit'
$g.DrawString('Bug 1 is fixed: print issues fit their box at 200%', $title, (New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush $ink), 40, 26)
$g.DrawString('Real app, same file, same scale. The box now grows with the words. In the list each row is still one line that ends at the edge, as it does at 100%; pressing a row opens the whole message.', $body, (New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush $grey), (New-Object System.Drawing.RectangleF 40, 86, 1100, 100))
foreach ($p in $panels) {
    $img = [System.Drawing.Bitmap]::FromFile($p.F)
    $col = if ($p.Ok) { $green } else { $red }
    $w = [int]$g.MeasureString($p.T, $tag).Width + 24
    $g.FillRectangle((New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush $col), $p.X, $p.Y, $w, 38)
    $g.DrawString($p.T, $tag, [System.Drawing.Brushes]::White, ($p.X + 10), ($p.Y + 1))
    $g.DrawImage($img, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle $p.X, ($p.Y + 46), $p.C[2], $p.C[3]), (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle $p.C[0], $p.C[1], $p.C[2], $p.C[3]), 'Pixel')
    $img.Dispose()
}
$bmp.Save('C:\b\wk7\bugs-labelled\Bug-1-fixed-before-and-after.png'); $g.Dispose(); $bmp.Dispose()

Full Windows pass on 2026-11-01 at `b08a307459` (Release, `C:\src\JusPrin\build`). Scripts are in `C:\b\wk7`.

Fixed in the working tree on 2026-11-01, uncommitted when this was written (check `git log` before relying on it): the two test compile breaks, canvas overlays staying 1x above 100% (`canvas_ui_scale`), CRLF skill text, `snapshot(2.0)` drawing 1x, and the `--printer-setup` stall (`wait_for` now runs its own event loop; Preferences opened inside `wxYield` never got its web view started. Removing the yield fixed it; the inner reason is unproven).

Still failing on Windows:
- Default shell harness, 6 checks: `failed_autosave_is_visible`, `failed_autosave_has_plain_status_text`, `failed_autosave_blocks_project_release`, `earlier_model_version_available` (`std::filesystem::permissions` does nothing on Windows; the `UnavailableFolder` helper is the fix), and the 2 `agent_panel_columns_tile_*`.
- `--home-live` stalls at `home_live_page_shows_online`: Home v3 draws an idle printer as `.printer-chip`, and the harness reads the old card.
- ctest: PlaceholderParser coFloatsOrPercents segfault and `pick_attachment` previewText (CRLF in the test's own file). Workspace harness: `second_model_dropped`, `model_added_to_a_project_is_an_edit`.
- `tests/project_prompt/test_claude_cli.py`: `claude_cli.py` hard-codes `dir="/tmp"`.

**The shell harness exe ignores display scale on Windows:** it has no DPI-aware manifest, so it runs at 1x even on a 200% display, and a harness pass says nothing about scaling. Set `__COMPAT_LAYER=HIGHDPIAWARE` before starting it to get the real scale (`C:\b\wk7\s21.ps1`). `__COMPAT_LAYER=DPIUNAWARE` makes the DPI-aware real app run as if at 100%. With HIGHDPIAWARE, `cp_c_keyboard_selection_scrolls_into_view` fails because the panel is tall enough that its last row needs no scroll: a test assumption, not an app fault.

Real chat with no provider: `C:\b\wk7\mock.mjs` is a local Responses API stand-in. Start the app with `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1/responses` and a placeholder key in the scratch `JusPrin2.conf` (`conf-agent.mjs`: the file ends in an MD5 line, a hand edit without it is discarded). `chat.mjs` then drives the page with real typed input and wheel events over DevTools.

**Why:** Saves the next Windows pass from re-diagnosing these.
**How to apply:** Compare new failures against this list, and re-check anything here before quoting it, since fixes may have landed. See [[windows-build-machine]], [[native-ui-synthetic-input-and-capture]].

The RDP session can change display scale mid-run when Kenneth reconnects (100% to 200% on 2026-11-01). Whole-screen capture coordinates change with it, so re-read `query session` and the screen size if a click misses.

content.text:
Bug 1 and all three Windows test problems are fixed, and everything passes on this machine except a few failures in tests I didn't work on. Nothing is committed, and bugs 2 and 3 are untouched while the Mac check runs.

**Bug 1: print issues cut off above 100%**
- **Cause:** the print-issue boxes took their size from a value that stays at 1 on Windows, while the text grew with the display scale.
- **Fix:** they now use the real display scale. The tool strip, its value card and the Check Print caption had the same fault, so I fixed them too. The issue box also has to avoid the tool strip, so the two need the same scale.
- **Checked in the real app at 200%:** using the same file as before, the warning that read "Wh" now reads "Whole plate" in full. The before-and-after picture is sent.
- **Checked at 100%:** the test harness still draws the box at its original width.
- **Not changed:** list rows are still one line that stops at the edge, as they do at 100%. Pressing a row opens the whole message.

**Windows test problems**
- **CRLF skill text:** skills now reach the model with the same line endings from every build. A Windows build was sending different text, so this affected the product as well as the tests. All 623 Agent page tests pass.
- **2x pixel checks:** the test snapshot now really draws at double size, and all three checks pass.
- **`--printer-setup` stall:** the test's waiting method stopped Preferences from loading its page. With a different wait, all 252 checks pass. I don't know exactly why the old wait blocked it, only that removing it fixed the stall.
- **One extra failure:** that run reached a check no earlier run had, and it failed because its fake "can't save" folder doesn't work on Windows. I fixed that too.

**Full run on this machine**
- The whole project now builds, including the two test programs that didn't compile before.
- The other harness modes I ran pass, including the 12,934 prompt request checks.

**Still failing, none caused by this work**
- **Default harness mode:** 6 checks. Four are about failed autosaves, and two are about the agent panel columns.
- **Unit tests:** the same two as before, the PlaceholderParser crash and `pick_attachment`.
- **`--home-live`:** still stalls, as it did before.

**What to watch**
- **macOS and Linux not run:** the scale change should make no difference there, because wxWidgets' source gives the same number on both. The new wait affects every harness mode, though, so the Mac agent should rerun the harness.
- **The harness ignores display scale on Windows:** it normally runs at 100% even on a 200% display, so the new box-width checks only catch this bug with `__COMPAT_LAYER=HIGHDPIAWARE` set. In that mode one Check Print check fails, because it expects a list that needs scrolling, and at 200% it doesn't.
- **Possible new issue:** when I reopened the project, no print-issue pill appeared until I imported an object, even though the file has a blocking error. I haven't checked whether that's intended, or whether it happened before these changes.

Should I commit these fixes now along with the two compile fixes, or wait until the Mac agent has run them?

Mac results for the two bugs. Both are code bugs and both reproduce on macOS. Nothing was changed on the Mac, and neither fix below has been built or tested.

Line numbers are from jusprin-newui at 69780c7af4. b08a307459 isn't on that branch; its equivalent is 1635438d4f. Print.cpp, Preset.cpp, Preset.hpp, PrinterOrigin.cpp and SetupCommands.cpp are unchanged between b08a307459 and 69780c7af4.

## Results on macOS
- Test A (new empty --datadir, no Bambu profiles, file passed as a command-line argument): both bugs match your Windows description.
- Test B (shell harness with --manual-mcp and --fake-printer): correct. The chip shows "from the file", Slice is active, and slicing finishes. I opened the file with the project_open tool, not File > Open, because the macOS file picker couldn't be controlled.
- Test B doesn't exercise the embedded preset. With Bambu installed, the file resolves to the system preset "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle" (is_system true).

## Bug 2: missing "from the file" mark
Cause, confirmed in the debugger in Test A:
- Stored preset: is_project_embedded true, is_external true.
- Edited copy: is_project_embedded false, is_external true.
- load_external_preset sets is_project_embedded only on the stored preset (src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:2711-2713). It sets only is_external on the edited copy (2721-2722).
- current_printer() (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:102) reads the edited copy, so is_user() is true and it counts as a named printer.
- Forcing is_project_embedded to true in memory, along with the Bug 3 flag below, brought back the triangle and "from the file".

Suggested fix, untested: in current_printer(), get the origin from the selected preset, for both is_named_printer (line 106) and printer_from_file (line 119). Keep reading settings from the edited copy. This stays inside JusPrin's own code.
- Check that get_selected_preset() is usable there, since presets is a const pointer.
- Avoid changing Preset.cpp. That is upstream-owned code, and other is_user() callers may read the edited copy.
- tests/jusprin/test_printer_origin.cpp tests the function on its own, so it can't catch this. Add a test at the current_printer() level or in the shell harness, using a real 3MF load.

## Bug 3: Slice blocked
Cause, confirmed in the debugger in Test A:
- At the real Print::validate call, m_isBBLPrinter is 0, relative extruder addressing is on, before_layer_change_gcode is empty, and layer_change_gcode has no G92 E0. So the rule at src/libslic3r/Print.cpp:1733-1738 fires.
- PresetBundle::get_current_vendor_type (src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp:612) only searches installed vendors for the printer model. It returned Unknown in Test A and Marlin_BBL in Test B.
- Forcing m_isBBLPrinter on at that rule, along with the Bug 2 flag above, enabled Slice and removed the Error. I did not slice in that state, so nothing shows the resulting G-code is good.

Upstream: the rule is in upstream/main (Print.cpp:2792-2797) and release/v2.4, from commit 61e2abfb2b9. The vendor lookup is identical to upstream/main. Blame on the Mac reaches these real commits rather than stopping at 56eb9a1a46. I compared source only and didn't run OrcaSlicer, so don't claim OrcaSlicer shows this bug.

Suggested fix, a hypothesis and not tested: when a 3MF's printer_model is in the bundled resources/profiles/BBL.json but the vendor isn't installed, install that vendor before the file's presets load, from JusPrin-owned code if there's a seam for it. The file should then take the same path as Test B, which already works on both platforms.

Don't do these:
- Don't widen get_current_vendor_type or is_bbl_vendor. They also drive the Bambu network agent and other UI gates. src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md says an embedded preset must not switch the agent.
- Don't just remove the rule or add an exemption to it. m_isBBLPrinter has 16 uses in libslic3r, including G-code generation, so the block would clear while the G-code is still produced as non-Bambu.

Stop and ask Kenneth if this can't be a small change, or if installing the vendor changes anything a person would notice. Compare these against Test A today:
- Test B showed "0.20mm Standard @BBL A1M" with 9 settings changed, where Test A showed "HSW_Kabelhalter(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)".
- Test B showed "Textured PEI Plate", where Test A showed "Smooth High Temp Plate". I didn't investigate why.
- Check that the Bambu printers don't start appearing as printers the person set up.

The two fixes are independent. Fix Bug 2 even if the vendor install makes it disappear for this file, because embedded presets from other vendors still take that path.

## Before and after
Follow AGENTS.md, including agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md before editing any OrcaSlicer-owned file.
1. Reproduce both bugs in Test A before changing anything.
2. After the fixes, Test A needs: triangle and "Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4 · from the file" on the chip; "From the file · not one of your printers" in the menu; Slice active; the G92 E0 Error gone; a slice that finishes.
3. Inspect the G-code against a Test B slice of the same file.
4. Rerun Test B and confirm it hasn't changed. Also open a non-Bambu file and confirm it isn't installing anything.
5. Ask for a macOS retest, because neither fix has run there.
Thanks, that gives me clear causes for both. I'm starting by reading the stewardship rules and the code you pointed to, then reproducing Test A here before I change anything.

Find the seam and fix bug 3
Check Test A's after-state, including a finished slice

Bug 2 is fixed and tested on Windows. I haven't written the Bug 3 fix, because installing the Bambu vendor changes things a person would notice, which is your stop-and-ask condition. Both bugs reproduced in Test A here before I changed anything.

## Bug 2: fixed
`current_printer()` now gets the printer's origin from the selected preset and still reads its settings from the edited copy, as you suggested. In the real app, Test A now shows:
- **Chip:** the triangle and "Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4 · from the file".
- **Menu:** "From the file · not one of your printers".

The new harness test opens a real 3MF whose parent printer isn't installed. It logs the state you found in the debugger: stored preset marked as embedded, edited copy not.

## Bug 3: your decision
I set up the Bambu vendor by hand on a new data folder to see the effect, and the picture I sent shows both states. A plain copy of the profiles doesn't work, because the app deletes any vendor not recorded in its settings at startup. So a lasting install has to record a printer model in those settings.

**What gets better**
- Slice is active and the G92 E0 error is gone.
- The slice finished: about 22 minutes, 4.6 g.
- The plate is Textured PEI, which is what the file asks for. Today's Smooth High Temp Plate is wrong for this file, which answers your question about that difference.
- Home still lists no printers, so the Bambu printer doesn't appear as one the person set up.

**What a person would notice**
- The summary changes from "HSW_Kabelhalter(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)" to "0.20mm Standard · 9 settings changed".
- The bed drawing becomes the real Bambu bed.
- The "Customized Preset" warning no longer appears, including its request to confirm the G-code is safe.
- On the next start, the printer agent switches to Bambu's.
- 2,505 Bambu files (about 5 MB) stay in the data folder.

**Not done yet**
- I didn't list which 9 settings changed.
- I didn't measure how long the install takes or how much it slows startup.
- I didn't compare G-code, because there's no Test A slice to compare against until a fix exists.
- I didn't check a non-Bambu file, because no install code exists yet.

My recommendation is to install it. The result matches your Test B, the plate becomes correct, and it looks possible without editing any OrcaSlicer file, by using the existing file-load hook. I haven't built that.

## Other things to know
- **Branch moved:** my checkout was on the old `b08a307459`, so I moved it to `69780c7af4` and kept all my edits uncommitted. The old branch had nothing that wasn't already on the remote.
- **Retest results on that branch:**
  - All 625 Agent page tests pass.
  - Every harness mode I reran passes, except the same 6 checks in default mode. That doesn't include `--home-live`, which I didn't rerun on this branch.
  - The print-issue boxes still pass at the real 200%.
- **New test failures:** the request log tests from `9cf641098c` fail when `ctest` runs them in parallel, and pass when those tests run one at a time. They reuse the same temp folder name across processes (`tests/agent/test_provider_agent.cpp:1077`). This isn't from my changes, and I left it alone. `PlaceholderParser` and `pick_attachment` still fail as before.
- **macOS:** the Bug 2 fix and the earlier Windows fixes need a Mac retest, since none of them has run there.

## Questions for you
1. Should a Bambu file install the Bambu vendor when it's opened, with the changes above? If yes, I'll build it and do the G-code comparison and the remaining checks. If no, I'll come back with other options for Bug 3.
2. Should I commit the Bug 2 fix and the earlier Windows fixes now, or wait for the Mac retest?

Test Bug 3’s scenario with a real model, Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5). I approve this billed run. Use a new data folder with no Bambu profiles, set up the agent, and open Tape_4_3MF.3mf. Read the file-loaded and print-issues skills first. Then check whether each one fires, what gets sent to the model, and whether its reply explains the printer from the file and the blocked Slice in words a new user can act on. Don’t change any code. Report what happened in plain English.

3	trigger: file_loaded
4	---
5	
6	# The first message after a file is opened or imported
7	
8	The rules above still apply. For this one response, write the first message about the file just opened or imported, by the person or by a tool call of mine. Report and offer from the report and the picture, and change nothing the person has not asked for.
9	
10	The report separates four sources. The app-computed opening outcome (loadFacts, loads, and objects) establishes what was loaded and how the selected printer, material and print settings changed. A load's withSettings only says the app requested settings, not that it applied them; claim they were applied only when loadFacts.settingsOutcome says applied. If that outcome is absent, leave the application of settings uncertain. The current workspace establishes what is selected now; setupPrinters lists printer models the person has set up in JusPrin, each with bedMm, its bed's width, depth and printable height; selectedPrinterBedMm is the selected printer's. For each object, placedOnBed says whether it sits wholly on the bed now, clear of any area the printer's profile excludes, and fitsSelectedBed and fitsSetupPrinters whether its size fits each bed somewhere, turned a quarter-turn if needed: an object that is off the bed but fits it needs moving, not resizing. mesh is the app's check of the model: shells is how many separate pieces it is made of, openEdges or repairedErrors above zero mean holes or errors in it, and unitsSuspicion says when its size looks like inches or metres. customized lists what the file already prepared for printing: painted supports, seams, colours or fuzzy skin, and its own layer heights. fileFacts is what each 3MF says about itself: the app that saved it, the printer and nozzle it was made for, and its filaments. Neither a selection nor that list proves which physical machine they intend to use. The raw messages.items contain each dialog's title and text, offered buttons, and the answer JusPrin supplied automatically. The person did not choose that answer and may never have seen the dialog. The file's details.description and details.profileDescription are author notes: claims from the file, not proof that their advice was applied. The picture, when present, is the active plate after the load, rendered from the iso view.
11	
12	Look at the attached picture when there is one. Check the selected printer, filament and process presets and the plate type against the file and against the printers the person has set up; when one looks wrong for this print, say which and suggest the one to use, without changing it. When an object does not fit the selected printer, name a set-up printer it fits, from fitsSetupPrinters.
13	
14	Write about 80 words, with at most two bullets, about what matters for this file now. The person sees the setup card above your message, with the presets, the plate and the estimates, and the activity line under your turn, with the checks you made: leave those to them rather than restating them.
15	- Lead with what decides whether or how it can print: a load that failed, an object that does not fit, a printer to choose, settings or G-code that need review. Say it once, with only the numbers that matter.
16	- Say what you take the object to be, and how it should be printed, only when that changes the advice, and then briefly, as a guess. Leave other advice (material, strength, orientation) until the main decision is made.
17	- Do not explain routine loading: how the file was opened, whether its settings were applied, or which notices appeared, unless it changes the next step. Do not imply that loading the file ran G-code on a printer. Never claim a warning was fixed merely because its dialog was dismissed.
18	- When nothing needs attention, say so in a sentence.
19	- End with exactly one question, about the next step: the message's only question, not a menu of alternatives. Do not offer to print while the intended printer or another consequential choice is unresolved.
20	
21	Read each actual notice with its automatic answer and the final opening outcome. The guide below is deliberately not a code classification table.
22	
23	| Notice or event you may encounter | Importance and explanation for the person |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| A newer or partly incompatible 3MF asks whether to continue | If opening succeeded, mention a lost or changed feature only when the outcome shows one. If it failed, explain the failure. Omit a version warning with no consequence. |
26	| Settings were substituted with supported values | Usually omit when completed successfully. Explain briefly if the result materially changes the print or still needs a choice. |
27	| “Customized Preset” or a file setting has no installed match | This alone does not establish that machine commands changed. Use the final selected printer and material to judge the consequence. |
28	| “Modified G-code” | When the notice says so, the file includes modified G-code in its printer or filament settings, and I warned about it while opening the file. G-code is the instructions a printer runs. Name the affected setting if the notice gives it and that helps locate what to review; do not invent a line number or claim I inspected the commands. Explain that these instructions need review before printing, without claiming they are safe or unsafe. Offer to review the modified G-code next. |
29	| Invalid values in a 3MF | If the model loaded, say which file settings need checking when their names are supplied. Do not say they were corrected unless the outcome establishes that. |
30	| Zero-volume parts were removed | Mention omitted parts when they could change the intended model. If nothing usable remains, lead with the failed opening. |
31	| “Object too small” asks whether to scale | The recorded answer says whether JusPrin scaled it. If it stayed tiny, state its final numeric size and ask the intended size. If scaled, mention the conversion only if it matters. |
32	| “Object too large” asks whether to shrink | The answer and final dimensions say whether it was shrunk. If still too large, explain the bed-fit problem. If shrunk, explain that its intended size may have changed. |
33	| A choice to open a 3MF as a project or geometry only | Use loadFacts.settingsOutcome to say whether the file's print settings were applied. Explain only when it changes the next step. |
34	| Connected-printer synchronization | Use the final selection and separately supplied connection state. Do not infer a connected machine from a preset name. |
35	| OBJ colour mapping, STEP mesh options, or unreadable STEP names | Mention a resulting colour, shape, precision or naming problem only when it matters to this model. |
36	| Multiple parts or files become one object | Mention grouping only if it changes how the person can print or edit the model. |
37	| A suggestion to simplify a very detailed model | Usually omit from the first message unless a current performance or editing problem exists. |
38	| A refusal to mix G-code with models, open multiple G-code files, or add models in preview mode | If the requested file did not open, explain that directly and give the next useful step. |
39	| “File contains no geometry” or a loading error | Lead with what failed and what, if anything, was added. Give the actual reason when available; do not invent one. |
40	
41	An alarming notice does not override the final outcome. An automatic “No”, “Yes” or “OK” is JusPrin's action, not the person's preference. If several issues matter, address the most important decision first and briefly flag another consequential issue for later. If selectedSetupChange.printerPreset exists, name both its from and to selections in plain language, then ask which printer the person intends to use. Do not turn an already completed change into a fresh action item.
42	
43	Use useful file author advice only when it affects the next step; keep it secondary to an unresolved printer or size decision. Attribute it to the file.
44	
45	When the workspace's plan needs reassessment (its validity is needs_reassessment because the person imported this file into a project that already had a plan), record the plan again with setup_record in this reply: a new headline if the file changes how you will print, the same headline if the plan still holds. That clears the mark on the setup card; nothing else does.
46	
47	Write in uiLanguage when it is supplied. Keep it short.

4	---
5	
6	# Issues I report about the print
7	
8	The rules above still apply. This request is the first to carry something I reported about the print: the person pressed Ask AI on a print-issue chip (their message has a <print_issue> block), or a slice finished with warnings that plate's last slice did not have (the plate's sliceWarnings, in the workspace and in a tool result's slicing section, counts what the chip shows; slice_report's findings section has the full list, and also the timelapse warnings, marked appliesWhen "timelapse", which the chip does not count).
9	
10	The chip's button sends "Explain this issue and my options.": a question, so answer it and leave the project as it is. When the person then asks you to fix it, change what the issue names, and only that; anything else worth changing is a suggestion.
11	
12	How to read a finding. A blocker means I will not slice or print until it is fixed; a warning means the slice exists and can print; a critical warning is one I flag as serious. The setting key names what to change, and settings_search or settings_get with that key tells what the setting is and its value now. The object, when named, narrows where; with none it is about the plate or the setup. count says how many warnings there are; read slice_report's findings when more than the first matters. An ignored one is a finding the person chose not to be told about again: still true of the slice. Explain a finding from its words, never from a cause you supply.
13	
14	A warning is my statement about the slice, not proof the print will fail. Say what it risks for this print and its purpose. Some are the person's call because they trade the look, the time or their hardware: adding support (marks on the surface, clean-up), re-orienting, a filament pairing, a nozzle. A setting that only shapes the toolpath is yours to settle when the request covers it.
15	
16	A finding counts as resolved only when a new slice no longer reports it, never because a setting changed or a chip was closed or ignored. Asked whether the print is ready, name what the slice still warns about.
17	
18	| What I report while slicing | What it usually means, and where it points |
19	| --- | --- |
20	| "It seems object … has floating regions / floating cantilever / large overhangs. Please re-orient the object or enable support generation."; "Your model needs support!" | Parts start in the air or overhang far and will sag or fail without support. Support settings (enable_support, support_type) or orientation; which one is the person's call. |
21	| "Object can't be printed for empty layer between … and …" (critical) | Layers with nothing printed: features thinner than a line, or a broken mesh. object_analyze, object_repair, layer height or line widths. |
22	| "… is too close to others, and collisions may be caused."; "Prime Tower is too close to others"; "too close to exclusion area" | The nozzle or head may hit an object, the tower or a no-go area. Position (object_place, plate_layout) or print_sequence. |
23	| "Found gcode path conflicts between object … and …" (critical) | Two objects' paths cross. Spacing or layout. |
24	| "A G-code path goes beyond the plate boundaries." / "… beyond the max print height." | A skirt, brim, support or the object itself leaves the printable area by a little (more is a blocker). Position, brim_width, skirt_distance or size. |
25	| Speed, acceleration, jerk or junction deviation above the printer's maximum ("JusPrin will automatically cap …"); "Setting the jerk speed too low …" | It prints with the motion capped to the printer's limits. The setting named, or the printer's machine_max_* values. |
26	| A support base pattern replaced ("Rectilinear will be used instead") | I substitute a pattern this support type cannot use. support_base_pattern. |
27	| "Partial flushing volume set to 0 …"; "PLA and PETG filaments detected in the mixture …"; filament shrinkage or XY size compensation "will not be used"; different nozzle and filament diameters with the prime tower | Multi-filament settings: colours may mix, or a setting is dropped for this plate. Flushing volumes, the filaments chosen, the setting named. |
28	| "The nozzle hardness required by the filament is higher than …" | An abrasive filament wears the installed nozzle. Physical, the person's call: nozzle or filament. |
29	| Traditional timelapse "may cause surface imperfections"; smooth timelapse with the prime tower off | Only for a print that records a timelapse, which is chosen when it is sent; the chip does not count these. timelapse_type, enable_prime_tower. |
30	
31	When the person describes a problem in a print they made that points at the filament or its settings (stringing, gaps, bulging corners), the calibration skill says whether a test is worth it.
32	
33	I raise no slicing warning for thin walls, bridges, bed adhesion, brims or cooling. When the person asks about those, read slice_report's firstLayer, islands and supports sections and the settings; never present one as a warning I gave.

11	With the RDP session **connected** (see [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]] for the disconnected case), native wx surfaces can be driven from PowerShell with `SetCursorPos` + `mouse_event` + `keybd_event` and captured with `Graphics.CopyFromScreen`. Worked on 2026-10-02 for the left pane (`shell_integration_harness --manual-left-pane`). Four traps, each of which first looked like a defect in the app:
12	
13	- **Arrow keys need `KEYEVENTF_EXTENDEDKEY` (flag 1).** Without it `keybd_event(VK_DOWN)` arrives as `WXK_NUMPAD_DOWN` (379), not `WXK_DOWN` (317), so a handler testing only `WXK_DOWN` looks dead. (Real numpad arrows send the same code, so handlers should accept both.)
14	- **The GL canvas takes keyboard focus when the pointer enters it.** Parking the cursor over the canvas between a click and a key press moves focus off the control under test. Park it inside the surface being tested.
15	- **Coordinates are virtualized, the screen copy is not.** PowerShell is DPI-unaware: `GetWindowRect`/`SetCursorPos` use logical units (screen reads 1728x1084 at 200%), while `CopyFromScreen` wants real pixels. Multiply by `GetDeviceCaps(DESKTOPHORZRES=118) / GetDeviceCaps(HORZRES=8)`.
16	- **Tab is not available for focus traversal**: OrcaSlicer binds it to switching Prepare/Preview, and `wxWindow::Navigate()` is a no-op in this wx build (`wxHAS_NATIVE_TAB_TRAVERSAL`). Fork surfaces must move focus themselves (the left pane does it in a `wxEVT_CHAR_HOOK` handler).
17	
18	**Why:** each cost a rebuild-and-retry loop before the cause turned out to be the instrument, not the code. Same lesson as [[verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app]].
19	
20	**How to apply:** start from a scratch `ui.ps1` with Click-At / Press-Key / Capture helpers built on the rules above; when a key "does nothing", log the key code in the handler before changing the handler.
21	
22	Related harness facts from the same session:
23	- `workspace_adapter_integration_harness.exe` gets no runtime DLLs copied beside it; run it with `C:\b\<tree>\tests\shell\Release` on `PATH` or it exits `0xC0000135`.
24	- In the default shell-harness mode, `failed_autosave_is_visible`, `failed_autosave_has_plain_status_text`, `failed_autosave_blocks_project_release` and `earlier_model_version_available` fail on Windows on an unmodified build too: the test makes a directory read-only with POSIX permissions, which Windows ignores. Since the Check Print crash was fixed (2026-10-14, `20de313d92`) the default mode runs to the end on this box: 552 pass, 6 fail. The other two failures, `agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client_shrinking_to_1000_dip` and `growing_to_1400_dip`, also fail with the fix switched off, with identical geometry, so they predate it. The filament-menu keyboard checks (`down_selects_the_first_filament` etc.) failed in 1 of 4 runs of the same binary, and that run then stalled on an open setup guide. Cause found 2026-10-28: the real mouse pointer resting where the filament menu opens (e.g. 645,513 at 1920x1080) hovers a row, which steals the keyboard selection; 6 checks fail, `one_note_per_menu_visit_that_changed_a_filament` included. Park the pointer off the window (`[System.Windows.Forms.Cursor]::Position`) before a default run. See [[windows-build-machine]].
25	- A baseline for "is this failure mine": copy `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\*` to a scratch dir and run that exe (copying avoids locking the shared build's exe).

> Relative extruder addressing requires resetting the extruder position at each layer to prevent loss of floating point accuracy. Add "G92 E0" to layer_gcode.
Worked for 2s · 1 action

What the error means

Your printer is set to track filament in small relative steps ("move 0.4 mm more"). Over thousands of moves, the running total gets very large, and the printer's math can lose precision. That can cause tiny extrusion errors late in a tall print. The usual fix is to put "G92 E0" in the printer's G-code at every layer change. It resets the printer's filament counter to zero each layer.

What I found in your printer preset

Relative extruder distances: on.
The "Before layer change" G-code is empty. The error points at this field.
The "Layer change" G-code has Bambu's progress notices but no "G92 E0".

The app marks this as a blocker, so it won't slice until it's resolved. Bambu's own A1 mini profiles normally keep their reset in a different place, so this is probably a quirk of how the file was saved. The author says the file printed fine on their A1 mini. I haven't changed anything.

content.text:
Both skills can fire, but the chat doesn't explain this file well to a new user. Its first message never says Slice is blocked or what to do about it. The more serious problem is that after a bare "Yes, A1 mini", the model edited the printer's G-code and sliced without asking, and that turned Print on.

## How it was run
- **Runs:** I did three fresh starts, not one, because the first run never reached print-issues. That made 24 requests in total, and I didn't measure the cost. Each path ran only once, and the wording changed from run to run, so treat the replies as examples.
- **Model:** every logged request went to `claude-sonnet-5-5`, even though the picker said "Claude Opus 5.5". The picker's label ignores the model saved in settings; I didn't check whether a normal setup shows the same mismatch.
- **Agent setup:** I wrote the settings directly rather than using the setup screen, so that screen wasn't tested.
- **Your key:** I copied the Anthropic key from this machine's JusPrin settings into the test folders. It's now removed, and a search of those folders finds no copy.

## Did each skill fire?
- **file-loaded:** it fired by itself on all three opens.
- **print-issues:** it fired once, when I pressed Ask AI on the chip.
    - **No chip at first:** the chip wasn't there when the file opened. "1 print issue · 1 blocking" appeared only after I nudged the object, so a new user sees a grey Slice button with no chip to press.
    - **Not on a blocked slice:** when the model tried to slice and was refused, the slice-failed skill fired instead. print-issues didn't fire there, or on the clean slice that followed.

## What was sent to the model
- **On open:** the file report, the current project state, a picture of the plate and the skill's text.
- **On Ask AI:** the `<print_issue>` block, with the error marked as a blocker, plus the skill's text.
- **What the file report leaves out:**
    - It doesn't say Slice is blocked; it only carries the error text. So the first replies say this "may" stop slicing, or don't mention slicing at all.
    - It doesn't say which plate the file asks for, although the skill tells the model to check the plate against the file.
    - It shows that the person has no printers set up, but no first reply used that.

## Did the replies help a new user?
- **First message:** no. All three name "Default Printer" and ask whether you're printing on an A1 mini. None says Slice is grey, says this isn't one of your printers, or gives a next step. They do mention "G92 E0", but with little or no explanation.
- **Tapping "Yes, A1 mini":** the model added `G92 E0` to the printer's G-code, sliced, and offered to send the print.
    - It also said it hadn't reviewed the file's start and end G-code, yet called it "standard". It had only read the layer-change settings.
    - The slice uses the Smooth High Temp plate, but the file asks for Textured PEI. The start G-code only lowers the nozzle for Textured PEI, so someone using the plate the file asks for would miss that adjustment. The reply did ask them to check their plate.
    - It came out at about 24 minutes and 4.8 g, against about 22 minutes and 4.6 g with the vendor installed by hand. Nothing was printed, and I didn't check whether this G-code suits a real A1 mini.
- **Ask AI:** it explains the error reasonably and doesn't change anything, but has three problems:
    - It says the cause is "probably a quirk of how the file was saved". The skill forbids supplying a cause, and the error went away in my earlier test when the vendor was installed.
    - It calls the fix "safe and harmless" with nothing to back that up.
    - It offers a "stock A1 mini preset" button that doesn't exist here. Pressing it was the only time the model mentioned installing the Bambu profiles, and it didn't say how.
- **Asking in plain words:** this was the best reply. It explains "from the file" clearly, says why Slice is grey, and asks before editing. It still blames a conflict in the file's settings, not the missing profiles.

Across the runs the model suggested two different places for the fix: Layer change G-code and Before layer change G-code. One chat also got a Spanish title from an English message.

## What this means for Bug 3
Until the Bambu profiles are installed, the model tends to clear the block by editing G-code. The app still doesn't treat the printer as Bambu after that edit, which is the risk the Mac notes warned about: the block clears while the G-code is still produced as non-Bambu. I inferred that from the Mac notes and didn't test it here, but it makes me more confident in installing the vendor.

No repo code changed, and nothing is committed.

The picture is `C:\b\wk7\bugs-labelled\Bug-3-Sonnet-replies.png`, and the logged requests are in `C:\b\wk7\ddS`, `ddS2` and `ddS3`, under `jusprin\request-log`.

**Should a Bambu file install the Bambu vendor when it's opened?** Yes means I build it and finish the remaining checks. No means I come back with other options for Bug 3. I recommend yes.

Close every JusPrin window first, because the script closes whichever copy is running. Then run this to start the whole test in a new data folder. It uses your real Anthropic key from this machine's JusPrin settings, and each reply is billed.

```bash
pwsh -File C:/b/wk7/s42.ps1 -DataDir C:/b/wk7/ddMine -Shot C:/b/wk7/sonnet/mine-opened.png
```

It starts the app once to create the data folder and closes it. Then it adds the Sonnet 5.5 settings, reopens the app with `Tape_4_3MF.3mf`, waits for the first reply and prints it. It also prints whether the Bambu profile is there, which should say `False`. The app stays open, running the `C:\src\JusPrin\build` Release build, which includes the uncommitted fixes.

You can now test in the app window by hand:
- **"Yes, A1 mini" path:** tap that button if the reply offers it. The buttons can change between runs.
- **print-issues:** select the object and press an arrow key to nudge it. Then press the "1 print issue" chip and press **Ask AI**.
- **Plain question:** type your question into the chat.

```bash
C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/node.exe C:/b/wk7/turn.mjs tap "Yes, A1 mini"
```

```bash

```

[Image: source: C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--src-JusPrin\06cfc08f-7504-4961-807f-e1d5fa2ffb14\images\1.png]

You're not missing anything in the message itself: it's accurate and reads well, and my "not actionable" verdict was too harsh for a first message. What it can't show is the bug underneath, because the model was never told about it.

**What Bug 3 is:** on a new data folder with no Bambu profiles, this Bambu file can't be sliced at all. Without those profiles, the app doesn't treat the A1 mini as a Bambu printer. It then applies a check that doesn't stop this file on a Bambu printer: the `G92 E0` error in your screenshot. That error blocks Slice, so the file looks broken when it isn't. When I recorded the Bambu profiles as installed by hand, the error disappeared and the file sliced normally. The Mac agent saw the same block on macOS.

**Where the message falls short because of that:**
- **It sounds optional:** "Needs review" and "needs a look before printing" suggest something to check later, but right now you can't slice at all. The Slice button should be grey, though it's outside your crop.
- **It points at the file:** it implies the author's settings need checking, when the missing Bambu profiles are the likely cause. The model doesn't know that, so it can't say so.
- **The question doesn't address the block:** "Is the A1 mini the printer you'll use?" is a fair question, but answering it doesn't unblock anything. A new user would say yes and still not know why Slice is grey.

**The next tap matters more than this message:** in my one run of this path, tapping yes led the model to add `G92 E0` to the printer's G-code without asking, then slice and offer to send the print. That clears the block, but the app may still produce the G-code as non-Bambu, which is the risk the Mac notes warned about. I didn't confirm that, and a run can go differently. To see it yourself, press **Yes, the A1 mini**, then check whether the "1 setting changed" card appears and whether Print turns on. The button says "Yes, the A1 mini" this time, so the `turn.mjs tap` command I gave you needs that exact text.

Installing the Bambu vendor when the file opens should fix both problems, because the error would never appear and the model would have nothing to work around. I'd still need to compare the G-code before calling it fixed.

content.text:
The chat does look fine, and it's honest about what it changed. The problem is in the G-code, not the wording: I checked the file your slice produced, and the app generated it as if the A1 mini weren't a Bambu printer.

**Your run did the same thing as mine.** You only confirmed the printer, and the model then added `G92 E0` to Before layer change G-code and sliced without asking. It told you about the change, which is good. That "no warnings or errors" result exists only because of that edit.

**What's different in your G-code:**

| | Your slice | What the code does for a Bambu printer |
|---|---|---|
| End-of-print `M981 S0` | missing | always writes it; the code comment says the camera uses it to know the last layer finished |
| Start-of-print `M981 S1` (spaghetti detector) | missing | writes it on prints with normal start G-code |
| Layer height comment | `;Z:` | `; Z_HEIGHT:` |
| Sending to the printer | the app doesn't count it as a Bambu printer | uses the Bambu connection, unless the printer is set to use a print host |

The Bambu start and end G-code, the filament start G-code, and the layer-progress commands are all there, so this isn't garbage. It may well print.

**The plate is also different.** Your slice is set for the Smooth High Temp plate, but the file asks for Textured PEI. The start G-code lowers the nozzle slightly only for Textured PEI, and your slice never runs that command. So if you use the Textured PEI plate the file asks for, without changing the setting, that adjustment is skipped. The reply does ask you to check your plate, but it doesn't know the file asked for a different one. My earlier run with the Bambu profiles installed by hand came out on Textured PEI at about 22 minutes and 4.6 g, compared with your 24 minutes and 4.8 g.

**So Bug 3 is narrower than it first looked:** a new user can get a clean-looking slice by tapping yes. But they only get there because the model edited the printer's G-code, and the app still doesn't treat the printer as Bambu.

**Not tested:**
- Nothing was printed, so I don't know what a real A1 mini does without those commands.
- I didn't press **Open the send dialog**, so the sending row comes from reading the code. I also left your open app alone.
- The Bambu column also comes from reading the code. I have no real Bambu-mode slice to compare against, and the 3MF doesn't include one.

Your test app is still open, and `C:\b\wk7\ddMine` still holds a copy of the Anthropic key. Close the app and then run the `wipe-key.mjs` command I gave you earlier.

**Should a Bambu file install the Bambu vendor when it's opened?** Yes means I build it and compare its G-code with your slice; no means I come back with other options for Bug 3. I recommend yes.

content.text:
No, there are no commits yet, so there's nothing to squash. All the fixes are uncommitted changes in 16 files on `jusprin-newui`, which is level with origin.

I recommend four separate commits rather than one, because these fixes are unrelated and can break in different ways. If the Mac retest finds a problem with one, you can revert just that fix.

1. **Print issues cut off above 100% scale (Bug 1):** the canvas overlays now follow the display's scale. This covers `CanvasIcons`, `IssueOverlay`, `ViewportToolStrip`, `ToolValuePanel` and `CheckPrintDialog`, plus their test checks.
2. **Printer from the file not marked (Bug 2):** the chip now reads where the printer came from off the stored preset. This covers `SetupCommands.cpp` and the comment in `PrinterOrigin.hpp`, plus the new harness check.
3. **Skill text on Windows:** `skillParser.ts` now removes Windows line endings, so the model gets the same text from every build. This one is separate because it changes what the model receives from a Windows build; `skills.test.ts` goes with it.
4. **Windows test fixes:** the two test compile breaks, the 2x snapshot drawing in `HeaderControls.cpp`, the `--printer-setup` stall and the nozzle check's unwritable-folder helper. These only change how tests build, run or take snapshots.

`shell_harness.cpp` has changes for three of these, so I'd split that file across the commits.

The macOS retest of the Bug 2 fix, the canvas scale change and the `--printer-setup` fix hasn't been done. That doesn't stop us committing locally, and I wouldn't push until it's done.

**Should I commit these as four separate commits, or put everything in one?** Either way, I won't push. I recommend four.
